A_time.equation: CL(t) = CL_low + (CL1 - CL_low) x exp(-k_time x t), t in hours since the first dose

calibration.target: CAN-1004 day 11 AUC to 72 h, linear trapezoidal
calibration.reason: The target lies outside what the form can reach in the search range.

B_prior_dose.equation: CL(t) = CL_low + (CL1 - CL_low) x exp(-k_dose x D_prior(t)), where D_prior(t) is the total dose (mg/m2) of all doses given before the most recent dose at or before t

decision.rule: A form is recorded as carrying the day 1 to day 11 rise over to Ogawa 2008 if its primary endpoint is consistent under the primary reading. Robustness across readings and the secondary endpoints are reported with it.

post_hoc_not_in_plan.status: Descriptive, computed after the locked result; not part of the decision and not a test.
post_hoc_not_in_plan.why: To show where each form ends up at the top of its range and in the limit of large k.

not_this: Not a population PK model: no between-patient variability, no covariates, typical values only.
Not a mechanistic model of target binding; the falling clearance imitates the observed effect with an empirical function.
Not validation or qualification; one calibration study (n = 10) and one test study (n = 5 to 7 per dose).
Not a dosing or exposure prediction for any patient.
known_differences_and_weaknesses: Calibration uses two summary numbers from 10 patients (a clearance ratio and a mean AUC); the falling-clearance shape is assumed, not estimated.
The CAN-1004 day 11 clearance is a non-compartmental apparent clearance; using its ratio to day 1 as the asymptote of the model's elimination clearance is an assumption.
Ogawa is Japanese patients with 48 h sampling; CAN-1004 non-Japanese with 72 h sampling; assays and NCA settings differ.
Ogawa's day 11 / day 1 ratio is a mean of per-patient ratios (n = 5); the model gives one typical-value ratio.
Two forms are checked, so one passing by chance is more likely than with one form.
